h1: Triple Two Silom — Spacious Design Boutique on Silom Road, Walking Distance to Chulalongkorn Hospital
intro: If you need a hotel close to King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital that does not feel like a clinic-adjacent box room, Triple Two Silom is worth serious consideration. This 4-star boutique hotel — part of the Narai Hospitality Group that has called Silom home since 1968 — opened in 2002 with 75 rooms that run generously from 45 sqm upward. The aesthetic is quietly contemporary: warm hardwood floors, dark-wood furniture, crisp white linen. Walk to BTS Sala Daeng in about 10 minutes, then take the covered skywalk at Exit 5 straight to Chulalongkorn Hospital — total door-to-hospital roughly 13–14 minutes. Breakfast is included in most packages and consistently earns five-star praise from guests. Rates start from around THB 2,500 per night.

body.html: Triple Two Silom has been quietly earning loyal guests since 2002, when Narai Hospitality — the same group behind the iconic Narai Hotel that shaped Silom's skyline in 1968 — opened a boutique companion property at number 222, just a few doors down. The brief was simple: smaller, more personal, contemporary. The result is a hotel with 75 rooms across four floors that punches above its price point in the areas guests care about most — space, cleanliness, and breakfast.

The rooms are the first thing reviewers mention. Deluxe and Premier rooms run 45 sqm; Junior Suites reach 60 sqm — proportions that feel generous in central Bangkok at this price tier. Warm oak-toned hardwood floors, dark wood furniture and framed artwork create an atmosphere that reads as premium without being flashy. Every room comes with a 49-inch Smart TV, minibar, bathrobes and slippers, and 24-hour room service. Bathrooms are a particular highlight: marble surrounds, a full-size bathtub and separate shower, and copper mosaic tiling on the vanity walls add a touch of boutique luxury that guests notice immediately.

"The room was much larger than expected — beautifully furnished, very clean, and the bed was excellent. The breakfast buffet could seriously compete with any five-star hotel: eggs made to order, freshly baked pastries, imported cheeses, smoked salmon. Great value."

Breakfast at Triple Two Silom has a reputation that travels well beyond TripAdvisor. Guests describe it as genuinely five-star in scope: Thai and Western options, eggs cooked fresh to order, artisanal pastries, imported cheeses, smoked salmon, and fresh juice. For families managing a hospital stay nearby, a proper hot breakfast — included in most rate plans — can make the difference between a manageable day and a draining one.

The walking route to King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital (Thai Red Cross Society) deserves its own paragraph for anyone staying here for medical reasons. Leave the hotel, turn right on Silom Road, and walk roughly 10 minutes to BTS Sala Daeng station. At Exit 5, a covered skywalk — sheltered from rain and sun — leads directly into the hospital compound in another 3–4 minutes. Total: around 13–14 minutes on foot. If the walk feels too long or the weather is unkind, Grab cars are available in front of the hotel around the clock and reach the hospital in about 5 minutes.

One honest point worth knowing before you book: the swimming pool is not in the Triple Two Silom building itself. Guests use the pool at the adjacent Narai Hotel, a 1970s-era landmark, which means a short walk next door and — because the pool is shared between two hotels — it tends to be busier than a private pool would be. Several reviewers noted the pool area feels dated, which is accurate given the Narai's heritage. If a private, resort-style pool matters to your stay, this is the detail that will disappoint. If pool access is secondary, it barely registers.

The surrounding neighbourhood is calm by Silom standards — away from the late-night bars of Soi 4 and Patpong, which are each a 10–15 minute walk. Street food, tailors, cafes, and the Sri Mariamman Temple (a vivid Hindu shrine just 200 metres away) provide texture without noise. MRT Si Lom and BTS Chong Nonsi are both within 10 minutes' walk, making the rest of Bangkok easy to reach. Overall scores hover around 8.7 out of 10 across more than 900 verified reviews — a consistent signal that guests leave satisfied.

honestSummary: Triple Two Silom delivers on its four-star promise: large, beautifully kept rooms, a genuinely impressive breakfast, and discreet, personal service in a quiet stretch of Silom Road that is close enough to everything — including King Chulalongkorn Hospital — without the noise. The honest caveat is the pool: it lives next door at the older Narai Hotel and is shared between both properties. If pool access ranks high on your list, know this going in. If it does not, this hotel consistently over-delivers for its price.
honestChecks: If a proper pool matters to you — the pool is at the 1970s-era Narai Hotel next door, is shared between two hotels, and feels dated. If you want a private, resort-style pool in your building, look at newer properties in the area instead.

If you need BTS right outside the door — it is a genuine 10-minute walk to Sala Daeng or Chong Nonsi. Fine on a dry day, but on a rainy Bangkok afternoon you will want Grab. Grab is available in front of the hotel at all times.

If you are visiting Chulalongkorn Hospital for a long stay — the Junior Suite at 60 sqm with a separate sitting area is well worth the upgrade. The extra space makes a multi-night medical stay significantly more comfortable, and the covered BTS skywalk route to the hospital is a genuine advantage.

tips.title: Fastest Route to Chulalongkorn Hospital
tips.body: Walk Silom Rd to BTS Sala Daeng (~10 min) → take the covered skywalk at Exit 5 directly into the hospital compound (~3–4 min). Total: 13–14 minutes on foot. If raining, Grab from the hotel takes about 5 minutes and costs under THB 60.

tips.title: Upgrade to Junior Suite for Multi-Night Stays
tips.body: At 60 sqm with a separate sofa area, the Junior Suite transforms a hospital-adjacent stay into something actually comfortable. Worth the premium if you are here for several nights supporting a patient.

tips.title: Do Not Skip Breakfast
tips.body: The buffet consistently earns praise well above what a four-star price implies — eggs to order, fresh pastries, imported cheeses, smoked salmon. Many rate plans include it; verify at booking time. Starting a hospital day with a proper meal here makes a real difference.

tips.title: Getting Around Silom and Beyond
tips.body: BTS Sala Daeng and Chong Nonsi are both about 10 minutes on foot — connections to Siam, Asok, and the Sukhumvit strip. MRT Si Lom adds interchange options. Patpong night market, street food, and Lumphini Park are all within walking distance or a short Grab ride.

faq.q: How far is Triple Two Silom from King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital?
faq.a: Walk along Silom Road to BTS Sala Daeng in about 10 minutes, then use the covered skywalk at Exit 5 to reach the hospital entrance in another 3–4 minutes — total approximately 13–14 minutes on foot. The skywalk is sheltered from rain and sun. A Grab car from the hotel to the hospital takes around 5 minutes. MRT Si Lom Exit 2 also connects via skywalk to the hospital.

faq.q: What room types does Triple Two Silom offer, and what do they cost?
faq.a: Three main types: Deluxe Room (45 sqm, from approx. THB 2,500/night), Premier Room (45 sqm with better views, from approx. THB 3,200), and Junior Suite (60 sqm with separate sitting area, from approx. THB 4,500). Rates vary by season and package — many include breakfast. Compare across Agoda, Booking.com and the hotel direct before booking.

faq.q: Does Triple Two Silom have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes, but the pool is located at the adjacent Narai Hotel, the sister property next door. Guests walk over to use it. The Narai Hotel is a historic 1970s building, so the pool area has an older feel, and it tends to be busy as it serves guests from both hotels. If a private in-building pool is important to you, this is worth knowing before you book.

faq.q: Is Triple Two Silom a good choice for families with a patient at Chulalongkorn Hospital?
faq.a: It is one of the better options in the area. The 45 sqm rooms are genuinely spacious — far larger than budget options nearby — with a full sofa, writing desk, and proper-size bathroom. The Junior Suite at 60 sqm is worth considering for stays of several nights. Free parking, 24-hour room service, and a strong breakfast make logistics easier. The covered BTS skywalk route to the hospital is particularly useful on rainy days.

faq.q: Which BTS and MRT stations are closest to Triple Two Silom?
faq.a: BTS Sala Daeng (Silom Line) and BTS Chong Nonsi (Silom Line) are both roughly 10 minutes on foot. MRT Si Lom is also about 10 minutes away. BTS Sala Daeng is the most useful for reaching the hospital. From Sala Daeng you can connect to Siam, Asok, and the full BTS network.
